thread:
Carmen L: Heads-up: NovaClaims POC is failing in the last-mile demo. Their SPA logs `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` when connecting to our streaming endpoint. Demo at 10:30 PT.

Ethan V: ok can you grab the request id + whether they're using EventSource or fetch stream? and any raw response sample?

Carmen L: request=nova-poc-20260402-7, client=Fetch + ReadableStream in Chrome. They attached a raw capture: shows `data: {\"id\":2,\"msg\":\"Payment processed \uD83D` then next chunk `\uDE4C\"}`

Riley K: looks like a UTF surrogate pair split across chunks. Also seeing several `499` and `502` in access logs around same time. Could be runtime flushing mid-codepoint or an intermediate proxy re-chunking.

InfraBot: Log bundle uploaded: https://s3.redwood/logs/nova-poc-20260402-7.tar.gz :file_cabinet:

Ethan V: two short repros: 1) curl -N to capture raw SSE and hexdump for byte boundaries, 2) run a small Node fetch that prints chunk lengths. If the bytes cut a multibyte utf8 sequence, it's server-side.

Carmen L: they ran curl and hexdump; confirms split at byte boundary inside the emoji UTF-8 sequence. They also reported spikes when opening 4+ simultaneous streams.

Riley K: concurrent streams hypothesis makes sense: worker flush policy may cut buffer when under pressure. Short-term fixes: - ask customer to lower concurrent streams for demo - provide client-side accumulator snippet to tolerate partial JSON - for hosted, we can flip org-level flag to disable aggressive flush/compression.

Ethan V: client snippet (minimal):
```js
const reader = resp.body.getReader(); const dec = new TextDecoder(); let buf=''; async function loop(){ while(true){ const {done,value} = await reader.read(); if(done) break; buf += dec.decode(value,{stream:true}); while(buf.indexOf('\n\n')>-1){ const ev = buf.slice(0, buf.indexOf('\n\n')); buf = buf.slice(buf.indexOf('\n\n')+2); const payload = ev.split(/\r?\n/).filter(l=>l.startsWith('data:')).map(l=>l.slice(5)).join(''); try{ const o = JSON.parse(payload); /* handle */ }catch(e){ /* wait for more */ } } } } loop();
```

Carmen L: sending that to NovaClaims now. They prefer not to change client but ok for demo.

Riley K: infra changes: ensure response chunks align with UTF-8 boundaries or only flush after a full `\n\n` event. Nginx fronting notes: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;` Also set `Cache-Control: no-transform`.

Ethan V: created ticket RED-INF-4975: "sse: prevent mid-codepoint chunk flush under load" assigned to eng-runtime. Priority P1.

InfraBot: RED-INF-4975 created and linked to log bundle.

Carmen L: For the demo we reduced their concurrency to 2 streams and applied client accumulator. Demo completed with degraded perf but no parse errors. NovaClaims asked for timeline for a permanent fix.

Riley K: estimate: small runtime guard behind flag in 48-72hrs, full reg test for Dedicated/Private ~1 week. We'll follow up in ticket with PR and test plan.

Carmen L: thanks everyone. I'll close loop with NovaClaims and attach the raw hexdump + ticket link.

Ethan V: adding to presales playbook: quick triage checklist for streaming POCs: 1) ask for raw hexdump, 2) check concurrency, 3) verify headers (Content-Encoding/Transfer-Encoding), 4) try curl -N, 5) provide client accumulator snippet, 6) escalate to RED-INF if needed.
